lecture_title: Building a Black Hole and the Near-Horizon Puzzle

assets.name: lecture_05_figure_02.png
assets.rationale: The upper compactified Minkowski wedge is complete, unobstructed, and legible. Adjacent frames preserve the same board state but place the lecturer closer to the diagram.
assets.subtitle_excerpt: We have the lower part of the diagram, which I won't draw.
assets.caption_hint: upper half of compactified radial Minkowski spacetime

assets.name: lecture_05_figure_03.png
assets.rationale: The developed eternal Schwarzschild diagram and the ordinary exterior coordinate grid are visible with minimal obstruction.
assets.subtitle_excerpt: There's r equals 6mg. r equals 100mg, far from the black hole.
assets.caption_hint: eternal Schwarzschild diagram with schematic constant-radius curves

assets.name: lecture_05_figure_05.png
assets.rationale: The null shell and the Schwarzschild region to be retained are visible without lecturer obstruction. This replaces the earlier transitional frame at 00:27:41, which contained no completed construction.
assets.subtitle_excerpt: Where now is inside the shell, and where is outside the shell?
assets.caption_hint: ingoing null shell on the Schwarzschild diagram

assets.name: lecture_05_figure_06.png
assets.rationale: The red collapse shell and green event horizon are both complete. Sampling at ten-second intervals from 00:37:00 through 00:39:50 confirmed that this frame best balances completed geometry and low obstruction.
assets.subtitle_excerpt: Nothing has happened there yet. The geometry is flat space.
assets.caption_hint: event horizon extending into the flat region before the shell arrives

assets.name: lecture_05_figure_07.png
assets.rationale: Both the asymptotic Hawking expression and the local formula T(rho)=1/(2 pi rho) remain legible after the derivation, with less obstruction than the writing sequence around 01:00:00.

assets.name: lecture_05_figure_08.png
assets.rationale: The completed microscope inequalities are legible together and the lecturer does not cover either relation.
assets.subtitle_excerpt: In what direction? Well, that direction is somewhat random.
assets.caption_hint: Heisenberg microscope resolution and momentum estimates

assets.name: lecture_05_figure_09.png
assets.rationale: The near-horizon layer, lambda less than rho, and the local energy estimate remain visible together after the derivation. Adjacent samples from 01:18:10 through 01:21:00 were inspected.
assets.subtitle_excerpt: You have to create exactly the conditions which the experiment was designed to show do not happen.
assets.caption_hint: near-horizon probe resolution and local energy

rejected_assets.reason: The lecturer blocks the central board and the image records only a transition between earlier diagrams, not the collapse construction.
